Daily Brief

The day's most significant developments center on escalating regional conflicts and diplomatic tensions. Bulgaria summoned Russia's ambassador after drone attacks sank a merchant ship in the Black Sea, leaving 11 crew missing—the latest in a series of strikes that NATO allies are monitoring closely [BBC, Le Monde, Financial Times]. The EU expressed cautious skepticism toward President Trump's proposed 'energy ceasefire' between Russia and Ukraine, with Kyiv reporting continued Russian strikes on energy infrastructure despite the announced deal [RFI]. In a dramatic political realignment, former DRC President Joseph Kabila announced he would lead a new 'politico-military' alliance with the M23 rebel group controlling eastern Congo, marking a significant escalation in his confrontation with President Tshisekedi's government [RFI]. Maritime security concerns intensified as Iran launched its worst spate of attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, targeting 24 vessels in two weeks [Financial Times], while the UK's MI5 chief warned of a 'major shift' in Iranian targeting of British military sites [Financial Times]. The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to ICJ Judge Navi Pillay, who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel committed genocide in Gaza—a selection likely to draw sharp international reactions [The Guardian].

01 Conflict

Bulgaria Summons Russian Ambassador After Drone Attack Sinks Ship, Leaves 11 Missing

  • Two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast; one sank 31km east of Krapets village with 11 crew missing and one rescued
  • Bulgarian PM Rumen Radev convened emergency meeting and summoned Russian ambassador, stating 'the logic suggests the outcome benefits the Russian Federation'
  • Russian ambassador Eleonora Mitrofanova denied having information from Moscow and suggested the strikes could be a 'third party provocation'
  • NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte spoke with Radev, pledging continued close work with Black Sea allies; this follows last week's sinking of the Alfa Watan which left 10 crew presumed dead

Former DRC President Kabila Announces Alliance with M23 Rebels to Overthrow Tshisekedi

  • Joseph Kabila, who ruled DRC from 2001-2019, unveiled the 'Front pour la Refondation de la Nation' at a press conference at his residence in M23-controlled Goma
  • The alliance's stated objective is to 'put an end to tyranny by any means, including force,' with Kabila as leader and senior M23 figures as deputies
  • Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia in 2025 after being convicted of 'complicity' with the Rwanda-backed M23 movement
  • The announcement represents a significant escalation, uniting one of DRC's most prominent political figures with an armed group controlling large areas of eastern Congo
